sights.n: Sanrio Puroland (サンリオピューロランド)
sights.address: Tama Center (Tama New Town), Tama, Tokyo — by Tama-Center Station (Keiō / Odakyū / Tama Monorail)
sights.w: Indoor theme park opened in 1990 in Tama New Town, half an hour from Shinjuku: a Hello Kitty musical, Kitty's house, live shows and meet-and-greets with My Melody, Cinnamoroll, Gudetama and Aggretsuko.
sights.anime: Hello Kitty & the Sanrio universe — the company's own indoor park ('Hello Kitty Land')

sights.n: Kamakurakōkōmae Railway Crossing — Slam Dunk (鎌倉高校前 踏切)
sights.address: By Kamakurakōkōmae Station (Enoden line), Koshigoe, Kamakura, Kanagawa
sights.w: The seaside Enoden level crossing just east of Kamakurakōkōmae Station, with the Pacific behind the passing tram — immortalised in the Slam Dunk opening and one of Japan's most-visited anime pilgrimage spots.
sights.anime: Slam Dunk — the railroad crossing from the anime's opening sequence

sights.n: Animate Ikebukuro Flagship Store (アニメイト池袋本店)
sights.w: Animate's flagship since 1983, expanded into ten floors of shops, event spaces, cafés and a theatre — recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's largest anime store, anchoring Ikebukuro's otaku quarter.
sights.anime: All franchises — Guinness-certified largest anime store, the hub of Ikebukuro's Otome Road scene

sights.n: Ultraman Shopping Street, Soshigaya (ウルトラマン商店街)
sights.address: North of Soshigaya-Ōkura Station (Odakyū line), Soshigaya, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
sights.w: The everyday shopping street running north from Soshigaya-Ōkura Station is decked out with Ultraman statues and street lamps — Tsuburaya Productions, the studio behind Ultraman, was headquartered nearby.
sights.anime: Ultraman — tokusatsu hero honoured by the street beside Tsuburaya Productions' former home

sights.n: Anime Tokyo Station, Ikebukuro (アニメ東京ステーション)
sights.w: Opened October 2023 as Tokyo's official anime hub: a free basement archive of ~50,000 production items — layouts, storyboards, original drawings and cels rarely shown publicly — plus rotating exhibitions.
sights.anime: Cross-franchise — the Metropolitan Government-backed anime archive (current shows: Digimon Adventure 02 & Ojamajo Doremi 25th anniversary)

sights.n: Tokyo Anime Center, DNP Plaza Shibuya (東京アニメセンター)
sights.address: DNP Plaza Shibuya 2F, Jinnan, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
sights.w: Formerly in Akihabara and then Ichigaya, the Tokyo Anime Center now runs rotating anime, manga and game exhibitions with AR/VR on the second floor of DNP Plaza Shibuya; the shop is free to enter.
sights.anime: Rotating franchise exhibitions — the long-running official anime promotion centre

sights.n: Toei Animation Museum, Ōizumi (東映アニメーションミュージアム)
sights.address: Toei Animation Ōizumi Studio, Higashi-Ōizumi, Nerima-ku, Tokyo
sights.w: Inside Toei Animation's Ōizumi studio in Nerima — the birthplace of Dragon Ball, Sailor Moon, One Piece and Pretty Cure — with exhibits on the studio's history and production.
sights.anime: Toei Animation — Dragon Ball, Sailor Moon, One Piece, Precure; museum in the working studio

sights.w: Tokyo's only natural ravine: a kilometre-long wooded path along the Yazawa River below street level, steps from Todoroki Station, ending at Todoroki Fudōson temple.
A riverside garden on the Edo River banks where some 50,000 irises of around 100 varieties bloom in June.

sights.n: Nihombashi Mitsukoshi Main Store (日本橋三越本店)
sights.w: Japan's first department store, descended from the 1673 Echigoya kimono shop; the 1935 building with its bronze lions and soaring atrium Tennyo (Goddess of Sincerity) statue is a nationally designated Important Cultural Property.
